passages.text: Later, Solomon formed an alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt by marrying his daughter. Solomon brought her to the City of David until he had finished building his palace and the house of the LORD, as well as the wall around Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
Pharaoh was king of Egypt.
Solomon formed an alliance with Pharaoh.
Solomon married Pharaoh’s daughter.
Solomon brought Pharaoh’s daughter to the City of David.
Solomon kept her there until he finished building his palace.
Solomon also built the house of the LORD.
Solomon built the wall around Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיִּתְחַתֵּ֣ן שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶת־ פַּרְעֹ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־ בַּת־ פַּרְעֹ֗ה וַיְבִיאֶ֙הָ֙ אֶל־ עִ֣יר דָּוִ֔ד עַ֣ד כַּלֹּת֗וֹ לִבְנ֤וֹת אֶת־ בֵּיתוֹ֙ וְאֶת־ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְאֶת־ חוֹמַ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סָבִֽיב׃

passages.text: The people, however, were still sacrificing on the high places because a house for the Name of the LORD had not yet been built.
passages.sermon: The people offered sacrifices on the high places.\r\nThey did this because there was no house built for the Name of the LORD.\r\nThis continued until those days.
passages.original: רַ֣ק הָעָ֔ם מְזַבְּחִ֖ים בַּבָּמ֑וֹת כִּ֠י לֹא־ נִבְנָ֥ה בַ֙יִת֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיָּמִ֥ים הָהֵֽם׃פ

passages.text: And Solomon loved the LORD and walked in the statutes of his father David, except that he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king of Israel.
Solomon loved the LORD.
Solomon followed the statutes of his father David.
Solomon sacrificed on the high places.
Solomon burned incense on the high places.
passages.original: וַיֶּאֱהַ֤ב שְׁלֹמֹה֙ אֶת־ יְהוָ֔ה לָלֶ֕כֶת בְּחֻקּ֖וֹת דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו רַ֚ק בַּבָּמ֔וֹת ה֥וּא מְזַבֵּ֖חַ וּמַקְטִֽיר׃

passages.text: Now the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for it was the great high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on the altar there.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
He went to Gibeon.
He went there to offer sacrifices.
Gibeon was the most important high place.
Solomon offered one thousand burnt offerings.
He placed these offerings on the altar at Gibeon.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ גִּבְעֹ֙נָה֙ לִזְבֹּ֣חַ שָׁ֔ם כִּ֥י הִ֖יא הַבָּמָ֣ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֑ה אֶ֤לֶף עֹלוֹת֙ יַעֲלֶ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה עַ֖ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֥חַ הַהֽוּא׃

passages.text: One night at Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream, and God said, “Ask, and I will give it to you!”
passages.sermon:
Solomon was the king of Israel.
One night, Solomon was at Gibeon.
The LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream.
God spoke to Solomon.
God said, "Ask for what you want me to give you."
God promised to give Solomon what he asked.
passages.original: בְּגִבְע֗וֹן נִרְאָ֧ה יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶל־ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בַּחֲל֣וֹם הַלָּ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים שְׁאַ֖ל מָ֥ה אֶתֶּן־ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Solomon replied, “You have shown much loving devotion to Your servant, my father David, because he walked before You in faithfulness, righteousness, and uprightness of heart. And You have maintained this loving devotion by giving him a son to sit on his throne this very day.
passages.sermon:
Solomon spoke to God.
Solomon said, “You showed great loving devotion to David, my father.
David was Your servant.
David walked before You in faithfulness.
David lived in righteousness.
David had an upright heart with You.
You kept this great loving devotion for David.
You gave David a son to sit on his throne today.
I am that son.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אַתָּ֨ה עָשִׂ֜יתָ עִם־ עַבְדְּךָ֙ דָוִ֣ד אָבִי֮ חֶ֣סֶד גָּדוֹל֒ כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ הָלַ֨ךְ לְפָנֶ֜יךָ בֶּאֱמֶ֧ת וּבִצְדָקָ֛ה וּבְיִשְׁרַ֥ת לֵבָ֖ב עִמָּ֑ךְ וַתִּשְׁמָר־ ל֗וֹ אֶת־ הַחֶ֤סֶד הַגָּדוֹל֙ הַזֶּ֔ה וַתִּתֶּן־ ל֥וֹ בֵ֛ן יֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־ כִּסְא֖וֹ כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: And now, O LORD my God, You have made Your servant king in my father David’s place. But I am only a little child, not knowing how to go out or come in.
passages.sermon:
Solomon is speaking to the LORD his God.
The LORD made Solomon king after David, Solomon’s father.
Solomon is now king instead of David.
Solomon calls himself God’s servant.
Solomon says he is a young boy.
Solomon says he does not know how to go out or come in.
Solomon admits he lacks experience and understanding.
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י אַתָּה֙ הִמְלַ֣כְתָּ אֶֽת־ עַבְדְּךָ֔ תַּ֖חַת דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑י וְאָֽנֹכִי֙ נַ֣עַר קָטֹ֔ן לֹ֥א אֵדַ֖ע צֵ֥את וָבֹֽא׃

passages.text: Your servant is here among the people You have chosen, a people too numerous to count or number.
passages.sermon:
Solomon is speaking to God.
Solomon calls himself God's servant.
Solomon says he is among God's people.
God chose these people.
These people are very many.
No one can count them.
No one can number them because they are so numerous.
passages.original: וְעַ֨בְדְּךָ֔ בְּת֥וֹךְ עַמְּךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחָ֑רְתָּ עַם־ רָ֕ב אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא־ יִמָּנֶ֛ה וְלֹ֥א יִסָּפֵ֖ר מֵרֹֽב׃

passages.text: Therefore give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people and to discern between good and evil. For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?”
passages.sermon:
Solomon was the new king of Israel.
God had chosen Solomon to rule after David, his father.
Solomon spoke to God in prayer.
Solomon called himself God’s servant.
Solomon asked God for help.
Solomon said, “Give your servant an understanding heart.”
He wanted to judge God’s people well.
He wanted to know the difference between good and evil.
Solomon said, “Who can judge your great people?”
He knew the people were many and important.
He knew he needed wisdom from God to lead them.
passages.original: וְנָתַתָּ֨ לְעַבְדְּךָ֜ לֵ֤ב שֹׁמֵ֙עַ֙ לִשְׁפֹּ֣ט אֶֽת־ עַמְּךָ֔ לְהָבִ֖ין בֵּֽין־ ט֣וֹב לְרָ֑ע כִּ֣י מִ֤י יוּכַל֙ לִשְׁפֹּ֔ט אֶת־ עַמְּךָ֥ הַכָּבֵ֖ד הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Now it pleased the Lord that Solomon had made this request.
passages.sermon:
The Lord saw what Solomon asked.
The Lord felt pleased.
Solomon made this request to the Lord.
The Lord approved Solomon’s request.
passages.original: וַיִּיטַ֥ב הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י אֲדֹנָ֑י כִּ֚י שָׁאַ֣ל שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: So God said to him, “Since you have asked for this instead of requesting long life or wealth for yourself or death for your enemies—but you have asked for discernment to administer justice— behold, I will do what you have asked. I will give you a wise and discerning heart, so that there has never been nor will ever be another like you.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Solomon.
God said, “You asked for wisdom to judge my people.
You did not ask for a long life for yourself.
You did not ask for riches for yourself.
You did not ask for the death of your enemies.
You asked for understanding to judge rightly.
I will do what you asked.
I give you a wise and understanding heart.
No one before you has been like you.
No one after you will be like you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֵלָ֗יו יַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁאַ֜לְתָּ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה וְלֹֽא־ שָׁאַ֨לְתָּ לְּךָ֜ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֗ים וְלֹֽא־ שָׁאַ֤לְתָּ לְּךָ֙ עֹ֔שֶׁר וְלֹ֥א שָׁאַ֖לְתָּ נֶ֣פֶשׁ אֹיְבֶ֑יךָ וְשָׁאַ֧לְתָּ לְּךָ֛ הָבִ֖ין לִשְׁמֹ֥עַ מִשְׁפָּֽט׃ הִנֵּ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתִי כִּדְבָרֶ֑יךָ הִנֵּ֣ה׀ נָתַ֣תִּי לְךָ֗ לֵ֚ב חָכָ֣ם וְנָב֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּמ֙וֹךָ֙ לֹא־ הָיָ֣ה לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְאַחֲרֶ֖יךָ לֹא־ יָק֥וּם כָּמֽוֹךָ׃

passages.text: Moreover, I will give you what you did not request—both riches and honor—so that during all your days no man in any kingdom will be your equal.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Solomon.
God said, “I will give you more than you asked for.
You did not ask for riches.
You did not ask for honor.
But I will give you riches.
I will give you honor.
No king will be like you during your life.
No one among the kings will be your equal as long as you live.”
passages.original: וְגַ֨ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ שָׁאַ֙לְתָּ֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לָ֔ךְ גַּם־ עֹ֖שֶׁר גַּם־ כָּב֑וֹד אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹא־ הָיָ֨ה כָמ֥וֹךָ אִ֛ישׁ בַּמְּלָכִ֖ים כָּל־ יָמֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: So if you walk in My ways and keep My statutes and commandments, just as your father David did, I will prolong your days.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Solomon.
God gave Solomon a condition.
God said, "If you walk in My ways,
and if you keep My statutes and commandments,
just as your father David walked,
then I will make your life long."
God promised to prolong Solomon's days if Solomon obeyed Him.
passages.original: וְאִ֣ם׀ תֵּלֵ֣ךְ בִּדְרָכַ֗י לִשְׁמֹ֤ר חֻקַּי֙ וּמִצְוֺתַ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלַ֖ךְ דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֑יךָ וְהַאַרַכְתִּ֖י אֶת־ יָמֶֽיךָ׃ס

passages.text: Then Solomon awoke, and indeed it had been a dream. So he returned to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then he held a feast for all his servants.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was the king of Israel.
He had a dream from God.
Solomon woke up.
He realized it was a dream.
Solomon went to Jerusalem.
He stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
He offered burnt offerings to God.
He also offered peace offerings.
Solomon held a feast.
He invited all his servants to the feast.
passages.original: וַיִּקַ֥ץ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֣ה חֲל֑וֹם וַיָּב֨וֹא יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֣ד׀ לִפְנֵ֣י׀ אֲר֣וֹן בְּרִית־ אֲדֹנָ֗י וַיַּ֤עַל עֹלוֹת֙ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ שְׁלָמִ֔ים וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּ֖ה לְכָל־ עֲבָדָֽיו׃פ

passages.text: At that time two prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.
passages.sermon: Two women came to the king.\r\nThese women were prostitutes.\r\nThey stood before the king.
passages.original: אָ֣ז תָּבֹ֗אנָה שְׁתַּ֛יִם נָשִׁ֥ים זֹנ֖וֹת אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖דְנָה לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: One woman said, “Please, my lord, this woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth while she was in the house.
passages.sermon:
Two women stood before King Solomon.
Both women were prostitutes.
One woman spoke to the king.
She said, “My lord, this woman and I live in the same house.
I gave birth while she was in the house.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֜אמֶר הָאִשָּׁ֤ה הָֽאַחַת֙ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י אֲנִי֙ וְהָאִשָּׁ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את יֹשְׁבֹ֖ת בְּבַ֣יִת אֶחָ֑ד וָאֵלֵ֥ד עִמָּ֖הּ בַּבָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also had a baby. We were alone, with no one in the house but the two of us.
passages.sermon:
Two prostitutes came to the king.
They stood before him.
One woman spoke to the king.
She said, “My lord, this woman and I live in the same house.
I gave birth while she was in the house.
On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also had a baby.
We were together in the house.
No one else was with us.
Only the two of us were in the house.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י בַּיּ֤וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי֙ לְלִדְתִּ֔י וַתֵּ֖לֶד גַּם־ הָאִשָּׁ֣ה הַזֹּ֑את וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ יַחְדָּ֗ו אֵֽין־ זָ֤ר אִתָּ֙נוּ֙ בַּבַּ֔יִת זוּלָתִ֥י שְׁתַּֽיִם־ אֲנַ֖חְנוּ בַּבָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: During the night this woman’s son died because she rolled over on him.
passages.sermon:
This woman had a son.
Her son died at night.
She lay on him during the night.
She caused his death by lying on him.
passages.original: וַיָּ֛מָת בֶּן־ הָאִשָּׁ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לָ֑יְלָה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁכְבָ֖ה עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: So she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from my side while I was asleep. She laid him in her bosom and put her dead son at my bosom.
passages.sermon:
Two women lived together in a house.
No one else was with them.
One woman gave birth to a son.
Three days later, the other woman also gave birth to a son.
One night, the second woman's son died.
She got up in the middle of the night.
I was sleeping.
She took my son from my side.
She laid my son in her bosom.
She put her dead son at my bosom.
passages.original: וַתָּקָם֩ בְּת֨וֹךְ הַלַּ֜יְלָה וַתִּקַּ֧ח אֶת־ בְּנִ֣י מֵֽאֶצְלִ֗י וַאֲמָֽתְךָ֙ יְשֵׁנָ֔ה וַתַּשְׁכִּיבֵ֖הוּ בְּחֵיקָ֑הּ וְאֶת־ בְּנָ֥הּ הַמֵּ֖ת הִשְׁכִּ֥יבָה בְחֵיקִֽי׃

passages.text: The next morning, when I got up to nurse my son, I discovered he was dead. But when I examined him, I realized that he was not the son I had borne.”
passages.sermon:
A woman woke up in the morning.
She wanted to nurse her son.
She found her son was dead.
She looked closely at the child in the morning.
She saw that this was not the son she had given birth to.
passages.original: וָאָקֻ֥ם בַּבֹּ֛קֶר לְהֵינִ֥יק אֶת־ בְּנִ֖י וְהִנֵּה־ מֵ֑ת וָאֶתְבּוֹנֵ֤ן אֵלָיו֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֛ה לֹֽא־ הָיָ֥ה בְנִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלָֽדְתִּי׃

passages.text: “No,” said the other woman, “the living one is my son and the dead one is your son.” But the first woman insisted, “No, the dead one is yours and the living one is mine.” So they argued before the king.
passages.sermon:
Two women stood before King Solomon.
One woman had lost her son.
The other woman had a living son.
The second woman spoke first.
She said, “No, the living child is my son.
The dead child is your son.”
The first woman replied.
She said, “No, the dead child is yours.
The living child is mine.”
They argued in front of the king.
passages.original: וַתֹּאמֶר֩ הָאִשָּׁ֨ה הָאַחֶ֜רֶת לֹ֣א כִ֗י בְּנִ֤י הַחַי֙ וּבְנֵ֣ךְ הַמֵּ֔ת וְזֹ֤את אֹמֶ֙רֶת֙ לֹ֣א כִ֔י בְּנֵ֥ךְ הַמֵּ֖ת וּבְנִ֣י הֶחָ֑י וַתְּדַבֵּ֖רְנָה לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: Then the king replied, “This woman says, ‘My son is alive and yours is dead,’ but that woman says, ‘No, your son is dead and mine is alive.’ ”
passages.sermon:
King Solomon sat as judge.
Two women stood before him.
Each woman claimed to be the mother of a living child.
The first woman said, “My son is alive.
Your son is dead.”
The second woman said, “No.
Your son is dead.
My son is alive.”
King Solomon repeated their words.
He said, “This woman says, ‘My son is alive and yours is dead.’
That woman says, ‘No, your son is dead and mine is alive.’”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ זֹ֣את אֹמֶ֔רֶת זֶה־ בְּנִ֥י הַחַ֖י וּבְנֵ֣ךְ הַמֵּ֑ת וְזֹ֤את אֹמֶ֙רֶת֙ לֹ֣א כִ֔י בְּנֵ֥ךְ הַמֵּ֖ת וּבְנִ֥י הֶחָֽי׃פ

passages.text: The king continued, “Bring me a sword.” So they brought him a sword, and the king declared, “Cut the living child in two and give half to one and half to the other.”
passages.sermon:
King Solomon sat as judge over two women.
Each woman claimed to be the mother of a living child.
One child was alive.
One child was dead.
King Solomon spoke.
He said, “Bring me a sword.”
The servants brought a sword to King Solomon.
King Solomon gave an order.
He said, “Cut the living child in two.”
He said, “Give half of the child to one woman.”
He said, “Give the other half to the other woman.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ קְח֣וּ לִי־ חָ֑רֶב וַיָּבִ֥אוּ הַחֶ֖רֶב לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ גִּזְר֛וּ אֶת־ הַיֶּ֥לֶד הַחַ֖י לִשְׁנָ֑יִם וּתְנ֤וּ אֶֽת־ הַחֲצִי֙ לְאַחַ֔ת וְאֶֽת־ הַחֲצִ֖י לְאֶחָֽת׃

passages.text: Then the woman whose son was alive spoke to the king because she yearned with compassion for her son. “Please, my lord,” she said, “give her the living baby. Do not kill him!” But the other woman said, “He will be neither mine nor yours. Cut him in two!”
passages.sermon:
The woman whose son was alive spoke to the king.
She was the true mother.
She felt deep compassion for her son.
She said, “Please, my lord, give her the living baby.
Do not kill him.”
The other woman said, “He will be neither mine nor yours.
Cut him in two.”
passages.original: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר הָאִשָּׁה֩ אֲשֶׁר־ בְּנָ֨הּ הַחַ֜י אֶל־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ כִּֽי־ נִכְמְר֣וּ רַחֲמֶיהָ֮ עַל־ בְּנָהּ֒ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר׀ בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֗י תְּנוּ־ לָהּ֙ אֶת־ הַיָּל֣וּד הַחַ֔י וְהָמֵ֖ת אַל־ תְּמִיתֻ֑הוּ וְזֹ֣את אֹמֶ֗רֶת גַּם־ לִ֥י גַם־ לָ֛ךְ לֹ֥א יִהְיֶ֖ה גְּזֹֽרוּ׃

passages.text: Then the king gave his ruling: “Give the living baby to the first woman. By no means should you kill him; she is his mother.”
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the ruler of all Israel.
He spoke to the people in his court.
He said, “Give the living baby to the first woman.”
He commanded, “Do not kill the child.”
He explained, “She is his mother.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר תְּנוּ־ לָהּ֙ אֶת־ הַיָּל֣וּד הַחַ֔י וְהָמֵ֖ת לֹ֣א תְמִיתֻ֑הוּ הִ֖יא אִמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When all Israel heard of the judgment the king had given, they stood in awe of him, for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to administer justice.
passages.sermon:
All the people of Israel heard the king’s judgment.
They saw what the king had done.
They stood in awe of the king.
They saw that God had given him wisdom.
They saw that he could do justice.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ כָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶת־ הַמִּשְׁפָּט֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁפַ֣ט הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיִּֽרְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י רָא֔וּ כִּֽי־ חָכְמַ֧ת אֱלֹהִ֛ים בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃ס
